target.title: feat(review): classify unrecoverable UX bugs as P0
target.body:
## TLDR

ClawSweeper currently treats some community-breaking UX failures as ordinary technical severity. This PR adds a narrow UX release-blocker rubric so an issue that blocks a non-technical first-time/community user from download, install, setup, auth, first useful run, or recovery becomes:

- `triagePriority: "P0"`
- `impact:ux-release-blocker`

It also adds `impact:ux-friction` for user-facing pain that creates support burden but does not fully block progress.

Closes #386.
Related: openclaw/openclaw#75947 and openclaw/openclaw#99141.

## Why This Matters

Technical teams often rank by implementation difficulty or subsystem severity. For a community product, the more important question is sometimes simpler: can a normal user keep going without opening a terminal, editing config, reading logs, or asking maintainers for help?

If the answer is no, the project has lost the user even if the root cause is technically "minor." This PR teaches ClawSweeper to preserve that user-experience reality in the priority signal.

## Rubric

| User-facing evidence | ClawSweeper classification |
| --- | --- |
| Download, install, update, setup, onboarding, auth/provider setup, first useful run, or recovery is blocked for a non-technical first-time/community user. | `P0` + `impact:ux-release-blocker` |
| Recovery requires terminal commands, config edits, logs, manual file edits, or maintainer/support intervention. | `P0` + `impact:ux-release-blocker` |
| The user can continue only by reading docs, guessing, or getting support, but progress is not fully blocked. | `P1` or `P2` + `impact:ux-friction` |
| Cosmetic confusion or fully recoverable in-product friction. | Normal `P2`/`P3`; no UX release-blocker label |

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Issue or bug report"] --> B{"Touches user journey?"}
  B -- "No" --> C["Use existing technical priority rubric"]
  B -- "Yes" --> D{"Blocks progress or recovery?"}
  D -- "Requires terminal/config/logs/manual files/support" --> E["P0 + impact:ux-release-blocker"]
  D -- "Docs/support/guessing workaround" --> F["P1/P2 + impact:ux-friction"]
  D -- "Recoverable inside product" --> G["Normal P2/P3"]
  E --> H["bestSolution/workReason recommends less-technical surface"]
  F --> H
  H --> I["Doctor button / Fix button / setup wizard / inline recovery / visible command launcher"]
```

## What Changed

- Added issue-only impact labels:
  - `impact:ux-release-blocker`
  - `impact:ux-friction`
- Updated the review prompt with the UX override table and less-technical recovery guidance.
- Updated the JSON decision schema so both `impactLabels` and `labelJustifications[].label` accept the new labels.
- Added focused tests so prompt/schema/label plumbing stay aligned.

## Evidence

Real local ClawSweeper review proof with this branch's prompt/schema:

```text
pnpm run review -- --local-only --target-repo openclaw/openclaw --item-number 98674 \
  --target-dir /Volumes/LEXAR/repos/worktrees/openclaw-main-local-review-75947 \
  --artifact-dir /Volumes/LEXAR/Codex/reports/clawsweeper-ux-priority-converter/2026-07-02/local-review-98674 \
  --codex-timeout-ms 600000 --verbose
```

Result excerpt from the generated report for `openclaw/openclaw#98674`, a macOS install/setup blocker:

```text
review_status: complete
decision: keep_open
confidence: high
triage_priority: P0
impact_labels: ["impact:ux-release-blocker"]
label_justifications: [{"label":"P0","reason":"The report blocks a first-time macOS setup/install path because the user cannot reach the onboarding action on a short screen."},{"label":"impact:ux-release-blocker","reason":"A non-technical first-time macOS user can be stuck before completing setup unless the window can be resized, moved, or fixed by code."}]
```

Calibration proof for the non-blocking tier:

```text
pnpm run review -- --local-only --target-repo openclaw/openclaw --item-number 75947 \
  --target-dir /Volumes/LEXAR/repos/worktrees/openclaw-main-local-review-75947 \
  --artifact-dir /Volumes/LEXAR/Codex/reports/clawsweeper-ux-priority-converter/2026-07-02/local-review-75947 \
  --codex-timeout-ms 600000 --verbose
```

The broad UX anchor `openclaw/openclaw#75947` classified as `P2 + impact:ux-friction`, not P0, because it describes recurring setup/configuration friction but not a proven fully blocked first-run path. That is intentional: the override is narrow enough to distinguish blocker evidence from general UX debt.

Local focused terminal proof from the Lexar worktree:

```text
pnpm run build
> tsgo -p tsconfig.json
```

```text
node --test test/pr-label-policy.test.ts test/decision-parser.test.ts --test-name-pattern "UX|priority|impact|labelJustifications"
tests 42
pass 42
fail 0
```

```text
pnpm run format:check
All matched files use the correct format.
```

The ClawSweeper review on this PR correctly caught the missing `labelJustifications[].label` schema enum propagation. Commit `b05b919` adds the two UX labels to that enum and extends the schema-alignment test so this specific regression is covered.

## Why This Fix Is Scoped Correctly

- It reuses existing ClawSweeper priority and impact-label plumbing instead of adding a new schema concept.
- It keeps ClawSweeper in a triage/review role: this PR does not claim the product UX is fixed.
- It asks the model to recommend a less-technical recovery surface when relevant, but leaves implementation choices to maintainers.
- It pairs with openclaw/openclaw#99141 so future reports include the recovery-path facts needed for this rubric instead of forcing ClawSweeper to infer them from vague issue text.

## Proof Boundary

This proves ClawSweeper can classify, validate, and label UX blockers. It does not repair OpenClaw's first-run UX, and it does not replace openclaw/openclaw#76034.

## Validation

- `pnpm install`
- `pnpm run build`
- `node --test test/pr-label-policy.test.ts test/decision-parser.test.ts --test-name-pattern "UX|priority|impact"`
- `node --test test/pr-label-policy.test.ts test/decision-parser.test.ts --test-name-pattern "UX|priority|impact|labelJustifications"`
- `pnpm run format:check`
- `node --test test/clawsweeper.test.ts --test-name-pattern "UX|priority|impact"`

## Reviewer Checklist

- Confirm `P0 + impact:ux-release-blocker` is the desired release-blocker signal.
- Confirm the threshold is limited to blocked progress or technical recovery paths.
- Confirm `impact:ux-friction` covers non-blocking but support-heavy UX pain.
- Confirm schema, prompt, parser, and label tests all accept the new labels consistently.
